units.zh: 明宗三后一妃：和武憲皇后曹氏生晉國公主；昭懿皇后夏氏生秦王從榮、湣帝；宣憲皇后魏氏，潞王從珂母也；淑妃王氏，許王從益之慈母也。
units.en: Mingzong had three empresses and one consort: Empress Hewuxian, Lady Cao, bore the Jin State Princess; Empress Zhaoyi, Lady Xia, bore Congrong, Prince of Qin, and the Last Emperor; Empress Xuanxian, Lady Wei, was mother of Congke, Prince of Lu; Chaste Consort Lady Wang was foster mother to Congyi, Xu Wang.
units.literal: Mingzong had three empresses and one consort: Empress Hewuxian, Lady Cao, bore the Jin State Princess; Empress Zhaoyi, Lady Xia, bore the Prince of Qin Congrong and the Last Emperor; Empress Xuanxian, Lady Wei, was mother of the Prince of Lu Congke; Chaste Consort Lady Wang was foster mother of Xu Wang Congyi.

units.zh: 曹氏、夏氏皆不見其世家。
units.en: Neither Lady Cao nor Lady Xia appears in the genealogies.
units.literal: Lady Cao and Lady Xia do not appear in the genealogies.

units.zh: 夏氏無封爵，明宗未即位前卒。
units.en: Lady Xia bore no noble title and died before Mingzong ascended.
units.literal: Lady Xia held no enfeoffed title; she died before Mingzong took the throne.

units.zh: 明宗天成元年，封楚國夫人曹氏為淑妃，追封夏氏晉國夫人。
units.en: In Mingzong's first year Tiancheng, Lady Cao of Chu was made Chaste Consort and Lady Xia was posthumously enfeoffed Lady of Jin.
units.literal: In Tiancheng 1 of Mingzong, Lady Cao of Chu was made Chaste Consort and Lady Xia was posthumously enfeoffed Lady of Jin.

units.zh: 長興元年，立淑妃為皇后，而夏氏所生二子皆已王，乃追冊為皇后，謚曰昭懿。
units.en: In Changxing 1 the Chaste Consort was enthroned as empress; as both of Lady Xia's sons were already princes, Xia was posthumously canonized empress with the posthumous name Zhaoyi.
units.literal: In Changxing 1 the Chaste Consort was enthroned empress; both sons born of Lady Xia were already princes, so she was posthumously made empress with posthumous name Zhaoyi.

units.zh: 魏氏，鎮州平山人也。
units.en: Lady Wei came from Pingshan in Zhenzhou.
units.literal: Lady Wei was a native of Pingshan in Zhenzhou.

units.zh: 初適平山民王氏，生子十歲矣。
units.en: She had first married a commoner of Pingshan named Wang and bore a son who was ten years old.
units.literal: She first married a commoner of Pingshan named Wang and had borne a son of ten years.

units.zh: 明宗為騎將，掠平山，得其子母以歸。
units.en: As a cavalry commander Mingzong raided Pingshan and brought the mother and child away.
units.literal: When Mingzong was a cavalry commander he raided Pingshan and took the mother and child home.

units.zh: 居數年，魏氏卒，葬太原。
units.en: Several years later Lady Wei died and was buried at Taiyuan.
units.literal: After several years Lady Wei died and was buried at Taiyuan.

units.zh: 其子是為潞王從珂。
units.en: Her son was Congke, Prince of Lu.
units.literal: Her son was Congke, Prince of Lu.

units.zh: 明宗時，從珂已王，乃追封魏氏為魯國夫人。
units.en: Once Congke was already a prince under Mingzong, Lady Wei was posthumously enfeoffed Lady of Lu.
units.literal: In Mingzong's time, when Congke was already a prince, Lady Wei was posthumously enfeoffed Lady of Lu.

units.zh: 廢帝即位，追尊魏氏為皇太后，議建陵寢，而太原石敬瑭反，乃於京師河南府東立寢宮。
units.en: The Deposed Emperor posthumously honored her as empress dowager and planned a mausoleum, but when Shi Jingtang rebelled at Taiyuan they built a resting palace east of Henan in the capital.
units.literal: When the Deposed Emperor took the throne Lady Wei was posthumously honored as empress dowager; they planned to build a mausoleum, but when Shi Jingtang rebelled at Taiyuan they erected a resting palace east of Henan prefecture in the capital.

units.zh: 清泰三年六月丙寅，遣工部尚書崔儉奉上皇太后寶冊，謚曰宣憲。
units.en: On bingyin in the sixth month of Qingtai 3 the Minister of Works Cui Jian presented the empress dowager's seals and patent; she was posthumously named Xuanxian.
units.literal: On bingyin of the sixth month, Qingtai 3, Minister of Works Cui Jian was sent to present the empress dowager's seals and patent; her posthumous name was Xuanxian.

units.zh: 明宗和武憲皇后曹氏昭懿皇后夏氏
units.en: Mingzong; Empress Hewuxian, Lady Cao; and Empress Zhaoyi, Lady Xia
units.literal: Mingzong and Empress Wuhe, Lady Cao; Empress Zhaoyi, Lady Xia

units.zh: 宣憲皇后魏氏
units.en: Empress Xuanxian, Lady Wei
units.literal: Empress Xuanxian, Lady Wei

units.zh: 淑妃王氏
units.en: Chaste Consort Lady Wang
units.literal: Shufei Lady Wang

units.zh: 淑妃王氏，邠州餅家子也，有美色，號「花見羞」。
units.en: Chaste Consort Lady Wang came from a cake-selling family in Binzhou; famed for her beauty, she was called “Flowers Hide from Shame.”
units.literal: Shufei Lady Wang was the daughter of a cake merchant in Binzhou; she had great beauty and was called “Flowers Hide from Shame.”

units.zh: 少賣梁故將劉鄩為侍兒，鄩卒，王氏無所歸。
units.en: Young, she was sold as a maid to Liu Yan, once a Liang general; when Yan died, she was left with nowhere to turn.
units.literal: In her youth she was sold as a handmaid to Liu Yan, a former general of Liang; when Yan died, Wang had nowhere to go.

units.zh: 是時，明宗夏夫人已卒，方求別室，有言王氏於安重誨者，重誨以告明宗而納之。
units.en: Lady Xia had just died and Mingzong sought a new consort; word of Wang reached An Chonghui, who brought her to Mingzong’s notice, and he took her in.
units.literal: At that time Lady Xia, Mingzong’s wife, had died and he was seeking another consort; someone spoke of Wang to An Chonghui, who told Mingzong and he took her in.

units.zh: 王氏素得鄩金甚多，悉以遣明宗左右及諸子婦，人人皆為王氏稱譽，明宗益愛之。
units.en: Wang had amassed a great fortune from Yan and lavished it on Mingzong’s staff and his daughters-in-law; praise for her spread, and Mingzong’s affection deepened.
units.literal: Wang had received much gold from Yan and gave it all to Mingzong’s attendants and his sons’ wives; everyone praised Wang, and Mingzong loved her all the more.

units.zh: 而夫人曹氏為人簡質，常避事，由是王氏專寵。
units.en: Lady Cao was plain-spoken and unassuming and usually kept out of palace business, so Wang held favor alone.
units.literal: Lady Cao was plain and modest in character and often stayed out of affairs, so Wang had the exclusive favor.

units.zh: 明宗即位，議立皇后，而曹氏當立，曹氏謂王氏曰：「我素多病，而性不耐煩，妹當代我。」
units.en: When Mingzong became emperor, the court debated the empress; Cao was the rightful choice. She told Wang: “I have been sick for years and cannot endure the burden—sister, you should take my place.”
units.literal: When Mingzong took the throne they debated making an empress; Cao was the one to be enthroned. Cao said to Wang: “I have long been ill and cannot bear trouble—sister, you should stand in my place.”

units.zh: 王氏曰：「后，帝匹也，至尊之位，誰敢幹之！」
units.en: Wang replied: “The empress is the emperor’s match and the highest seat under Heaven—who would dare grasp at it!”
units.literal: Wang said: “The empress is the emperor’s equal, the most exalted seat—who would dare seize it!”

units.zh: 乃立曹氏為皇后，王氏為淑妃。
units.en: Cao was enthroned as empress and Wang was made Chaste Consort.
units.literal: So Cao was enthroned empress and Wang was made Shufei.

units.zh: 妃事皇后亦甚謹，每帝晨起，盥櫛服御，皆妃執事左右，及罷朝，帝與皇后食，妃侍，食徹乃退，未嘗少懈，皇后心亦益愛之。
units.en: The consort served the empress with equal devotion: each dawn she attended Mingzong’s washing, combing, and dressing; after court she waited at their meals and withdrew only when they finished—never once slackening—and the empress came to love her in return.
units.literal: The consort also served the empress with great care: each morning when the emperor rose, washing, combing, and dressing were all tended by the consort at his side; after court, when emperor and empress ate, the consort waited on them and withdrew only after the meal—never slackening—and the empress’s heart grew fond of her as well.

units.zh: 然宮中之事，皆主於妃。
units.en: Yet within the palace, the consort held every thread of power.
units.literal: Yet palace affairs were all directed by the consort.

units.zh: 明宗病，妃與宦者孟漢瓊出納左右，遂專用事，殺安重誨、秦王從榮，皆與焉。
units.en: When Mingzong sickened, the consort and the eunuch Meng Hanqiong controlled who saw him; she ruled alone thereafter, and had a hand in the deaths of An Chonghui and Congrong, Prince of Qin.
units.literal: When Mingzong fell ill, the consort with the eunuch Meng Hanqiong managed his access; she then held sole power, and in killing An Chonghui and Prince of Qin Congrong she played a part.

units.zh: 劉鄩諸子，皆以妃故封拜官爵。
units.en: Liu Yan’s sons all received titles and posts through the consort’s favor.
units.literal: Liu Yan’s sons were all enfeoffed and given offices because of the consort.

units.zh: 湣帝即位，冊尊皇后為皇太后，妃為皇太妃。
units.en: When the Last Emperor succeeded, the empress became empress dowager and the consort imperial consort dowager.
units.literal: When the Last Emperor took the throne, the empress was elevated to empress dowager and the consort to imperial consort dowager.

units.zh: 初，明宗後宮有生子者，命妃母之，是為許王從益。
units.en: When a consort in Mingzong’s harem bore a son, he entrusted the boy to the consort to raise—this was Congyi, Xu Wang.
units.literal: Earlier, when a woman in Mingzong’s rear palace bore a son, he had the consort serve as foster mother—this was Xu Wang Congyi.

units.zh: 從益乳母司衣王氏，見明宗已老而秦王握兵，心欲自托為後計，乃曰：「兒思秦王。」
units.en: Congyi’s wet nurse, wardrobe attendant Lady Wang, saw Mingzong aging and the Prince of Qin commanding troops; scheming for her own future, she said: “The child longs for the Prince of Qin.”
units.literal: Congyi’s wet nurse, wardrobe attendant Lady Wang, saw Mingzong was old and the Prince of Qin held troops; intending to attach herself for the future, she said: “The boy misses the Prince of Qin.”

units.zh: 是時從益已四歲，又數教從益自言求見秦王。
units.en: Congyi was then four; she also drilled him to beg on his own to visit the Prince of Qin.
units.literal: By then Congyi was four; she also repeatedly taught Congyi to ask on his own to see the Prince of Qin.

units.zh: 明宗遣乳嫗將兒往來秦府，遂與從榮私通，從榮因使王氏伺察宮中動靜。
units.en: Mingzong sent the nurse to bring the boy to and from the Prince of Qin’s residence; she then colluded with Congrong, who set her to watch the palace.
units.literal: Mingzong sent the wet nurse to carry the child back and forth to the Prince of Qin’s mansion; she then had secret dealings with Congrong, and Congrong used Wang to spy on palace movements.

units.zh: 從榮已死，司衣王氏以謂秦王實以兵入宮衛天子，而以反見誅，出怨言。
units.en: After Congrong’s death, the wardrobe attendant insisted the Prince of Qin had marched in to protect the emperor and been killed as a traitor, and she began to complain aloud.
units.literal: After Congrong died, wardrobe attendant Wang claimed the Prince of Qin had actually entered the palace with troops to guard the Son of Heaven but was executed as a rebel, and she voiced grievances.

units.zh: 湣帝聞之，大怒，賜司衣王氏死，而事連太妃，由是心不悅，欲遷之至德宮，以太后素善妃，懼傷其意而止，然待之甚薄。
units.en: The Last Emperor heard, flew into a rage, and ordered the wardrobe attendant’s death; the affair implicated the consort dowager, and he turned against her. He meant to banish her to Zhide Palace, but held back lest he wound the dowager, who had always favored the consort—still, his treatment grew harsh.
units.literal: The Last Emperor heard, was furious, and granted wardrobe attendant Wang death; the matter touched the consort dowager, so his heart was ill pleased. He wished to move her to Zhide Palace, but stopped for fear of hurting the dowager, who had always been kind to the consort—yet he treated her very coldly.

units.zh: 廢帝入立，嘗置酒妃院，妃舉酒曰：「願辭皇帝為比丘尼。」
units.en: When the Deposed Emperor seized the throne, he once feasted in the consort’s quarters; she lifted her cup and said: “I beg to leave the emperor’s household and take the tonsure.”
units.literal: When the Deposed Emperor entered and took the throne, he once set wine in the consort’s compound; she raised her cup and said: “I wish to leave the emperor and become a Buddhist nun.”

units.zh: 帝驚，問其故，曰「小兒處偶得命，若大人不容，則死之日，何面見先帝！」
units.en: The emperor was startled and asked why. She said: “The boy barely kept his life; if Your Majesty will not spare us, when I die how shall I face the late emperor!”
units.literal: The emperor was startled and asked why; she said: “The boy barely escaped with his life; if Your Majesty does not bear with us, when I die how can I face the late emperor!”

units.zh: 因泣下。
units.en: And she wept.
units.literal: And she wept.

units.zh: 廢帝亦為之淒然，待之頗厚。
units.en: The Deposed Emperor was stricken too and treated her with new warmth.
units.literal: The Deposed Emperor was moved as well and treated her rather generously.

units.zh: 石敬瑭兵犯京師，廢帝聚族將自焚。
units.en: When Shi Jingtang’s army closed on the capital, the Deposed Emperor gathered his kin to die by fire.
units.literal: When Shi Jingtang’s troops threatened the capital, the Deposed Emperor gathered his clan and meant to burn themselves.

units.zh: 妃謂太后曰：「事急矣，宜少回避，以俟姑夫。」
units.en: The consort told the dowager: “All is lost—withdraw for now and wait for our uncle-by-marriage.”
units.literal: The consort said to the dowager: “Matters are urgent; you should withdraw a little and wait for our uncle-by-marriage.”

units.zh: 太后曰：「我家至此，何忍獨生，妹自勉之！」
units.en: The dowager answered: “Our house has come to this—how could I live on alone? Sister, save yourself!”
units.literal: The dowager said: “Our house has come to this—how can I bear to live alone? Sister, take care of yourself!”

units.zh: 太后乃與帝俱燔死，而妃與許王從益及其妹匿於鞠院以免。
units.en: The dowager burned with the emperor, while the consort hid with Congyi, Xu Wang, and his sister in the hospital ward and survived.
units.literal: The dowager then burned to death with the emperor, while the consort with Xu Wang Congyi and his sister hid in the hospital ward and escaped.

units.zh: 晉高祖立，妃自請為尼，不可，乃遷於至德宮。
units.en: When Jin Gaozu rose, the consort begged to become a nun but was denied and sent to Zhide Palace.
units.literal: When Jin Gaozu took the throne, the consort asked to become a nun but was refused; she was moved to Zhide Palace.

units.zh: 晉遷都汴，以妃子母俱東，置於宮中，高祖皇后事妃如母。
units.en: When Jin shifted the capital to Bian, the consort and the boy’s mother went east and were lodged in the palace; Gaozu’s empress honored the consort as a mother.
units.literal: When Jin moved the capital to Bian, the consort and the boy’s mother went east together and were housed in the palace; Gaozu’s empress treated the consort as a mother.

units.zh: 天福四年九月癸未，詔以郇國三千戶封唐許王從益為郇國公，以奉唐祀，服色、旌旗一依舊制。
units.en: On guiwei in the ninth month of Tianfu 4, an edict made Congyi, Xu Wang of Tang, Duke of Xun with three thousand households to keep the Tang rites; robes and banners followed the old forms.
units.literal: On guiwei, the ninth month of Tianfu 4, an edict enfeoffed Tang’s Xu Wang Congyi as Duke of Xun with three thousand households of Xun to maintain Tang sacrifices; dress and banners followed the old system.

units.zh: 太常議立莊宗、明宗、湣帝三室，以至德宮為廟；
units.en: The Ministry of Rites proposed three ancestral tablets—for Zhuangzong, Mingzong, and the Last Emperor—with Zhide Palace as the shrine;
units.literal: The Ministry of Rites proposed establishing three spirit tablets—for Zhuangzong, Mingzong, and the Last Emperor—with Zhide Palace as the temple;

units.zh: 詔立高祖、太宗，為五廟，使從益歲時主祠。
units.en: an edict added Gaozu and Taizong for five shrines and put Congyi in charge of the seasonal offerings.
units.literal: an edict added Gaozu and Taizong for five temples, with Congyi presiding at the seasonal rites.

units.zh: 出帝即位，妃母子俱還洛陽。
units.en: When the Deposing Emperor succeeded, the consort and her son returned to Luoyang.
units.literal: When the Deposing Emperor took the throne, the consort and mother and son all returned to Luoyang.

units.zh: 契丹犯京師，趙延壽所尚明宗公主已死，耶律德光乃為延壽娶從益妹，是為永安公主。
units.en: When the Khitan took the capital, Mingzong’s princess, Zhao Yanshou’s wife, was already dead; Yelü Deguang gave Yanshou Congyi’s sister as bride—she became Princess Yong’an.
units.literal: When the Khitan invaded the capital, Mingzong’s princess whom Zhao Yanshou had married was dead; Yelü Deguang had Yanshou marry Congyi’s sister—she became Princess Yong’an.

units.zh: 公主不知其母為誰，素亦養於妃，妃至京師主婚禮。
units.en: The princess never knew her mother; the consort had raised her from childhood, and when the consort reached the capital she oversaw the wedding.
units.literal: The princess did not know who her mother was; she had always been raised by the consort; when the consort reached the capital she presided over the wedding.

units.zh: 德光見明宗畫像，焚香再拜，顧妃曰：「明宗與我約為弟兄，爾吾嫂也。」
units.en: Deguang saw Mingzong’s portrait, burned incense, and bowed twice; turning to the consort he said: “Mingzong and I swore brotherhood—you are my sister-in-law.”
units.literal: Deguang saw Mingzong’s portrait, burned incense and bowed twice, turned to the consort and said: “Mingzong and I pledged brotherhood—you are my sister-in-law.”

units.zh: 已而靳之曰：「今日乃吾婦也。」
units.en: Then he amended: “Today you are my daughter-in-law.”
units.literal: Then he corrected himself: “Today you are my daughter-in-law.”

units.zh: 乃拜從益為彰信軍節度使，從益辭，不之官，與妃俱還洛陽。
units.en: He then named Congyi military governor of Zhangxin Circuit; Congyi refused the post and returned to Luoyang with the consort.
units.literal: He then appointed Congyi military governor of Zhangxin Circuit; Congyi declined and did not take office, returning to Luoyang with the consort.

units.zh: 德光北歸，留蕭翰守汴州。
units.en: Deguang marched north, leaving Xiao Han to guard Bianzhou.
units.literal: Deguang went north and left Xiao Han to hold Bianzhou.

units.zh: 漢高祖起太原，翰欲北去，乃使人召從益，委以中國。
units.en: When Han Gaozu rose at Taiyuan, Xiao Han prepared to withdraw north and sent for Congyi, entrusting him with the Middle Kingdom.
units.literal: When Han Gaozu rose at Taiyuan, Han meant to go north; he sent men to summon Congyi and entrusted him with China.

units.zh: 從益子母逃於徽陵域中，以避使者，使者迫之以東，遂以從益權知南朝軍國事。
units.en: Congyi and his mother fled into the grounds of Huiling to evade the envoys; pressed east, Congyi was made acting regent of the southern court’s armies and state.
units.literal: Congyi, mother and son fled into the grounds of Huiling to avoid the emissaries; the envoys pressed them east, and Congyi was made acting administrator of the southern dynasty’s military and state affairs.

units.zh: 從益禦崇元殿，翰率契丹諸將拜殿上，晉群臣拜殿下。
units.en: Congyi took the throne at Chongyuan Hall; Han led Khitan generals in bowing on the dais while Jin ministers bowed below.
units.literal: Congyi held court at Chongyuan Hall; Han led Khitan generals in bowing on the hall, Jin ministers bowing below the hall.

units.zh: 群臣入謁太妃，妃曰：「吾家子母孤弱，為翰所迫，此豈福邪？
units.en: The ministers came to pay court to the consort dowager; she said: “Our house—mother and son, weak and alone—forced by Han: is this fortune?
units.literal: The ministers came to visit the consort dowager; she said: “Our house, mother and son, weak and alone, forced by Han—is this blessing?

units.zh: 禍行至矣！」
units.en: Ruin is at hand!”
units.literal: Disaster is near!”

units.zh: 乃以王松、趙上交為左右丞相，李式、翟光鄴為樞密使，燕將劉祚為侍衛親軍都指揮使。
units.en: She made Wang Song and Zhao Shangjiao left and right chancellors, Li Shi and Zhai Guangye commissioners of military affairs, and the Yan general Liu Zuo commander of the palace guard.
units.literal: She made Wang Song and Zhao Shangjiao left and right chancellors, Li Shi and Zhai Guangye commissioners of military affairs, and Yan general Liu Zuo commander of the palace guard.

units.zh: 翰留契丹兵千人屬祚而去。
units.en: Han left a thousand Khitan soldiers under Liu Zuo and withdrew.
units.literal: Han left a thousand Khitan troops under Zuo and departed.

units.zh: 漢高祖擁兵而南，從益遣人召高行周、武行德等為拒，行周等皆不至，乃與王松謀以燕兵閉城自守。
units.en: Han Gaozu marched south; Congyi summoned Gao Xingzhou, Wu Xingde, and others to resist, but none came. He and Wang Song then planned to shut the gates and hold the city with Yan troops.
units.literal: Han Gaozu marched south with troops; Congyi sent to summon Gao Xingzhou, Wu Xingde, and others to resist; none came; he then plotted with Wang Song to shut the city with Yan troops and hold it.

units.zh: 妃曰：「吾家亡國之余，安敢與人爭天下！」
units.en: The consort said: “We are what remains of a ruined house—how dare we fight others for the realm!”
units.literal: The consort said: “We are remnants of a fallen dynasty—how dare we contend with others for the realm!”

units.zh: 乃遣人上書迎漢高祖。
units.en: She sent a memorial welcoming Han Gaozu.
units.literal: She sent men with a memorial welcoming Han Gaozu.

units.zh: 高祖聞其嘗召行周而不至，遣郭從義先入京師殺妃母子。
units.en: Gaozu heard they had called on Xingzhou in vain; he sent Guo Congyi ahead into the capital to kill the consort and her son.
units.literal: Gaozu heard they had summoned Xingzhou but he had not come; he sent Guo Congyi ahead into the capital to kill the consort and mother and son.

units.zh: 妃臨死呼曰：「吾家母子何罪？
units.en: Facing death, the consort cried: “What crime have we mother and son committed?
units.literal: At her death the consort cried: “What crime have we mother and son committed?

units.zh: 何不留吾兒，使每歲寒食持一盂飯灑明宗墳上。」
units.en: Why not spare my son, so each Cold Food Festival he may bring one bowl of rice to Mingzong’s grave?”
units.literal: Why not spare my son, so each year at Cold Food he may bring a bowl of rice to scatter on Mingzong’s grave?”

units.zh: 聞者悲之。
units.en: All who heard were moved to grief.
units.literal: Hearers were grieved.

units.zh: 從益死時年十七。
units.en: Congyi was seventeen when he died.
units.literal: Congyi died at seventeen.

units.zh: 湣帝哀皇后孔氏，父循，橫海軍節度使。
units.en: Empress Ai of the Last Emperor, Lady Kong, was daughter of Xun, military governor of Henghai.
units.literal: The Last Emperor's Empress Ai, Lady Kong—her father Xun was military governor of the Henghai army.

units.zh: 后有賢行，生四子。
units.en: The empress was known for virtue and bore four sons.
units.literal: The empress had virtuous conduct and bore four sons.

units.zh: 湣帝即位，立為皇后，未及冊命而難作。
units.en: When the Last Emperor succeeded she was named empress, but before the enthronement rites were finished disaster struck.
units.literal: When the Last Emperor took the throne she was made empress, but before the enthronement rites could be completed calamity arose.

units.zh: 湣帝出奔，后病子幼，皆不能從。
units.en: The Last Emperor fled; the empress was sick and the children too young to follow.
units.literal: The Last Emperor fled; the empress was ill and the children young—none could follow.

units.zh: 廢帝入立，后及四子皆見殺。
units.en: When the Deposed Emperor seized the throne, the empress and all four sons were put to death.
units.literal: When the Deposed Emperor entered and took the throne, the empress and all four sons were killed.

units.zh: 晉高祖立，追謚曰哀。
units.en: When Jin Gaozu rose he posthumously named her Ai.
units.literal: When Jin Gaozu took the throne he posthumously gave her the name Ai.

units.zh: 明宗子
units.en: Mingzong's Sons
units.literal: Mingzong's Sons

units.zh: 明宗四子，曰從璟、從榮、從厚、從益。
units.en: Mingzong had four sons: Congjing, Congrong, Conghou, and Congyi.
units.literal: Mingzong had four sons: Congjing, Congrong, Conghou, and Congyi.

units.zh: 從璟初名從審，為人驍勇善戰，而謙退謹敕。
units.en: Congjing was first named Congshen—fierce in battle, yet modest, careful, and self-restrained.
units.literal: Congjing was originally named Congshen; he was bold and skilled in battle, yet humble, cautious, and disciplined.

units.zh: 從莊宗戰，數有功，為金槍指揮使。
units.en: He campaigned with Zhuangzong, won repeated honors, and became commander of the Golden Spears.
units.literal: Campaigning with Zhuangzong he won repeated merit and became commander of the Golden Spears.

units.zh: 明宗軍變於魏，莊宗謂從璟曰：「爾父於國有大功，忠孝之心，朕自明信。
units.en: When Mingzong’s army mutinied at Wei, Zhuangzong told Congjing: “Your father has served the realm with great merit; I know his loyalty and filial heart for myself.
units.literal: When Mingzong’s troops mutinied at Wei, Zhuangzong told Congjing: “Your father has great merit to the state; his loyalty and filial devotion—I myself trust and know.

units.zh: 今為亂軍所逼，爾宜自往宣朕意，毋使自疑。」
units.en: Now mutineers press him; go yourself and speak my mind, lest he turn against himself.”
units.literal: Now the mutinous troops force him; you should go yourself to proclaim my intent, and do not let him doubt himself.”

units.zh: 從璟馳至衛州，為元行欽所執，將殺之，從璟呼曰：「我父為亂軍所逼，公等不亮其心，我亦不能至魏，願歸衛天子。」
units.en: Congjing raced to Weizhou, was seized by Yuan Xingqin, and faced execution; he cried: “Mutineers force my father; you do not see his heart—I cannot reach Wei; let me return to serve the Son of Heaven.”
units.literal: Congjing galloped to Weizhou, was seized by Yuan Xingqin, and was about to be killed; Congjing cried: “My father is forced by mutinous troops; you gentlemen do not understand his heart—I cannot reach Wei either; I ask only to return and serve the Son of Heaven.”

units.zh: 行欽釋之。
units.en: Xingqin let him go.
units.literal: Xingqin released him.

units.zh: 莊宗憐其言，賜名繼璟，以為己子。
units.en: Moved by his words, Zhuangzong renamed him Jijing and treated him as a son.
units.literal: Zhuangzong pitied his words, bestowed the name Jijing, and treated him as his own son.

units.zh: 從莊宗如汴州，將士多亡於道，獨從璟不去，左右或勸其逃禍，從璟不聽。
units.en: When Zhuangzong marched on Bianzhou, soldiers melted away on the road; Congjing alone stayed. Some urged him to flee, but he refused.
units.literal: When Zhuangzong went to Bianzhou, many officers and men deserted on the road; only Congjing did not leave; attendants sometimes urged him to flee disaster, but Congjing would not listen.

units.zh: 莊宗聞明宗已渡黎陽，復欲遣從璟通問。
units.en: Hearing Mingzong had crossed Liyang, Zhuangzong meant to send Congjing again as envoy.
units.literal: Zhuangzong heard Mingzong had crossed Liyang and again wished to send Congjing with messages.

units.zh: 行欽以為不可，遂殺之。
units.en: Xingqin forbade it and had him killed.
units.literal: Xingqin thought it impossible and then killed him.

units.zh: 明宗即位，贈太保。
units.en: When Mingzong succeeded, he posthumously made Congjing Grand Guardian.
units.literal: When Mingzong took the throne, he posthumously made him Grand Guardian.

units.zh: 嗚呼！
units.en: Alas!
units.literal: Alas!

units.zh: 無父烏生，無君烏以為生？
units.en: Without a father, how is one born? Without a lord, how does one live?
units.literal: Without a father, how does one live? Without a lord, how does one live?

units.zh: 而世之言曰：「為忠孝者不兩全。」
units.en: Yet people say: “Loyalty and filial piety cannot both be fulfilled.”
units.literal: Yet the world says: “One who is loyal and filial cannot fulfill both.”

units.zh: 夫豈然哉？
units.en: Is that truly so?
units.literal: Is that so?

units.zh: 君父，人倫之大本；
units.en: Lord and father are the great foundations of human bonds;
units.literal: Lord and father are the great roots of human relations;

units.zh: 忠孝，臣子之大節。
units.en: loyalty and filial piety are the supreme duties of subject and son.
units.literal: loyalty and filial piety are the great obligations of subject and son.

units.zh: 豈其不相為用，而又相害者乎？
units.en: How could they not serve each other—and instead destroy each other?
units.literal: How could they fail to work together yet harm each other?

units.zh: 抑私與義而已耳。
units.en: The difference is only private desire against public duty.
units.literal: It is only a matter of self-interest versus righteousness.

units.zh: 蓋以其私則兩害，以其義則兩得。
units.en: Follow private desire and both are ruined; follow duty and both are honored.
units.literal: With self-interest, both suffer; with righteousness, both are fulfilled.

units.zh: 其父以兵攻其君，為其子者，從父乎？
units.en: If a father raises arms against his lord, should the son follow the father?
units.literal: If the father attacks his lord with troops, as his son, follow the father?

units.zh: 從君乎？
units.en: Or follow the lord?
units.literal: Follow the lord?

units.zh: 曰：「身從其居，誌從其義，可也。」
units.en: The answer is: “Let the body stay where it stands, but let the will follow righteousness—that will do.”
units.literal: One says: “Let the body follow where it dwells, the intent follow righteousness—that is enough.”

units.zh: 身居君所則從君，居父所則從父。
units.en: If one stands with the lord, serve the lord; if with the father, serve the father.
units.literal: If the body dwells with the lord, follow the lord; if with the father, follow the father.

units.zh: 其從於君者，必辭其君曰：「子不可以射父，願無與兵焉！」
units.en: He who follows the lord must plead with him: “A son must not shoot at his father—I beg leave not to bear arms!”
units.literal: For one who follows the lord, he must tell the lord: “A son cannot shoot at his father—I beg not to take up arms!”

units.zh: 則又號泣而呼其父曰：「盍舍兵而歸我君乎！」
units.en: Then he weeps and cries to his father: “Lay down your arms and return to my lord!”
units.literal: Then he weeps and calls to his father: “Why not lay down arms and return to my lord!”

units.zh: 君敗則死之，父敗則終喪而事君。
units.en: If the lord falls, die with him; if the father falls, mourn him fully, then serve the lord again.
units.literal: If the lord is defeated, die with him; if the father is defeated, complete mourning then serve the lord.

units.zh: 其從於父者，必告之曰：「君不可以射也，盍舍兵而歸吾君乎！」
units.en: He who follows the father must tell him: “You must not shoot at the lord—lay down your arms and return to our lord!”
units.literal: For one who follows the father, he must tell him: “You cannot shoot at the lord—why not lay down arms and return to our lord!”

units.zh: 君敗則死之，父敗則待罪於君，赦己則終喪而事之。
units.en: If the lord falls, die with him; if the father falls, await judgment from the lord, and if spared, mourn fully and serve again.
units.literal: If the lord is defeated, die with him; if the father is defeated, await punishment from the lord, and if pardoned, complete mourning then serve him.

units.zh: 古之知孝者莫如舜，知義者莫如孔、孟，其於君臣父子之際詳矣，使其不幸而遭焉，其亦如是而已矣！
units.en: In antiquity none knew filial piety like Shun, none knew righteousness like Confucius and Mencius—they weighed every bond between lord and subject, father and son; had fate forced such a choice on them, they would have done no differently!
units.literal: Of those who knew filial piety in antiquity none surpass Shun; of those who knew righteousness none surpass Confucius and Mencius—they were thorough in the matters between lord and subject, father and son; had they unluckily met such a case, they would have acted just so!

units.zh: 從璟之於莊宗，知所從而得其死矣。
units.en: Congjing, facing Zhuangzong, knew where he stood—and met the death that was his due.
units.literal: Congjing toward Zhuangzong knew whom to follow and earned his death.

units.zh: 哀哉！
units.en: Alas!
units.literal: Alas!

units.zh: 秦王從榮，天成元年，以檢校司徒兼御史大夫，拜天雄軍節度使、同中書門下平章事。
units.en: Congrong, Prince of Qin—in Tiancheng 1 he was made Acting Minister of Education and Censor-in-Chief, military governor of Tianxiong, and Chief Minister.
units.literal: Congrong, Prince of Qin—in Tiancheng 1 was made Acting Minister of Education and concurrent Censor-in-Chief, appointed military governor of the Tianxiong army and Chief Minister.

units.zh: 三年，徙鎮河東。
units.en: In the third year he was transferred to Hedong.
units.literal: In the third year he was transferred to govern Hedong.

units.zh: 長興元年，拜河南尹，兼判六軍諸衞事。
units.en: In Changxing 1 he was made Governor of Henan and given charge of the Six Armies and palace guards.
units.literal: In Changxing 1 he was made Governor of Henan and concurrently judged the affairs of the Six Armies and palace guards.

units.zh: 從璟死，從榮於諸皇子次最長，又握兵柄。
units.en: After Congjing's death Congrong was eldest among the princes and held the army.
units.literal: When Congjing died, Congrong was eldest among the princes in order of birth and also held military power.

units.zh: 然其為人輕雋而鷹視，頗喜儒，學為歌詩，多招文學之士，賦詩飲酒，故後生浮薄之徒，日進諛佞以驕其心。
units.en: Yet he was quick-witted and sharp-eyed, fond of letters; he wrote verse, gathered scholars to drink and compose, and frivolous youths daily flattered him to feed his pride.
units.literal: Yet he was light and sharp in manner with a hawk's gaze; he delighted in Confucian learning, composed songs and poems, and gathered many literary men to versify and drink, so frivolous young men daily advanced flattery to swell his pride.

units.zh: 自將相大臣皆患之，明宗頗知其非而不能裁制。
units.en: Generals and ministers alike were alarmed; Mingzong knew his faults but could not check him.
units.literal: From generals and chancellors downward all were troubled; Mingzong knew well his faults but could not restrain him.

units.zh: 從榮嘗侍側，明宗問曰：「爾軍政之餘，習何事業？」
units.en: Once while Congrong stood beside him, Mingzong asked: "Apart from military duties, what do you study?"
units.literal: Once while Congrong attended at his side, Mingzong asked: "Besides military affairs, what studies do you pursue?"

units.zh: 對曰：「有暇讀書，與諸儒講論經義爾。」
units.en: He answered: "When I have time I read and debate the classics with scholars."
units.literal: He answered: "When I have leisure I read books and discuss the classics with scholars."

units.zh: 明宗曰：「經有君臣父子之道，然須碩儒端士，乃可親之。吾見先帝好作歌詩，甚無謂也。汝將家子，文章非素習，必不能工，傳於人口，徒取笑也。吾老矣，於經義雖不能曉，然尚喜屢聞之，其餘不足學也。」
units.en: Mingzong said: "The classics teach the bonds of lord and subject, father and son, but only great upright scholars are fit company. I saw the late emperor dote on verse—to no purpose. You are a soldier's son; letters are not your trade and you will not excel; let them circulate and you become a laughingstock. I am old; I may not grasp the classics, yet I still like to hear them—the rest is not worth your time."
units.literal: Mingzong said: "The classics hold the way of lord and subject, father and son, yet only great and upright scholars should be approached. I saw the late emperor fond of composing songs and poems—quite pointless. You are a general's son; writing is not your training and you cannot master it; spread by word of mouth it would only invite mockery. I am old; though I cannot grasp the classics, I still like to hear them often—the rest is not worth learning."

units.zh: 是歲秋，封從榮秦王。
units.en: That autumn Congrong was made Prince of Qin.
units.literal: That autumn Congrong was enfeoffed Prince of Qin.

units.zh: 故事，諸王受封不朝廟，而有司希旨，欲重其禮，乃建議曰：「古者因禘、嘗而發爵祿，所以示不敢專。
units.en: By custom a newly enfeoffed prince did not worship at the ancestral temple; but the officials, eager to please, proposed: “In antiquity titles and stipends were granted at the di and chang rites to show the throne did not act alone.
units.literal: By precedent, princes receiving enfeoffment did not attend the ancestral temple; but the officials, reading the emperor’s wish, wished to magnify the rite and proposed: “In antiquity, enfeoffment and stipend were granted at the di and chang sacrifices, to show one dared not act alone.

units.zh: 今受大封而不告廟，非敬順之道也。」
units.en: To receive so great an enfeoffment without informing the temple is not reverent obedience.”
units.literal: Now to receive great enfeoffment without reporting to the temple is not the way of reverent obedience.”

units.zh: 於是從榮朝服，乘輅車，具鹵簿，至朝堂受冊，出，載冊以車，朝於太廟，京師之人皆以為榮。
units.en: Congrong donned court robes, rode the state carriage with full guard, received the patent in the hall, then bore it by cart to the Grand Temple; the capital saw it as glory.
units.literal: So Congrong wore court dress, rode the state carriage, with full guard, received the patent at the court hall, went out, carried the patent by cart, and worshipped at the Grand Temple; people of the capital all took it for glory.

units.zh: 三年，加兼中書令。
units.en: In the third year he was also made concurrent Director of the Secretariat.
units.literal: In the third year he was additionally made concurrent Director of the Secretariat.

units.zh: 有司又言：「故事，親王班宰相下，今秦王位高而班下，不稱。」
units.en: The officials again said: “By custom princes stood below chancellors; the Prince of Qin outranks them yet sits lower—this ill becomes his station.”
units.literal: The officials again said: “By precedent, imperial princes ranked below chancellors; now the Prince of Qin’s rank is high yet his place in court is low—this does not fit.”

units.zh: 於是與宰相分班而居右。
units.en: He was therefore ranked apart from the chancellors and seated on the right.
units.literal: So he was given a separate rank from the chancellors and placed on the right.

units.zh: 四年，加尚書令，食邑萬戶。
units.en: In the fourth year he was also made Director of the Department of State Affairs, with a fief of ten thousand households.
units.literal: In the fourth year he was additionally made Director of the Department of State Affairs, with a fief of ten thousand households.

units.zh: 太僕少卿何澤上書，請立從榮為皇太子。
units.en: He Ze, vice director of the Master of Horses, memorialized the throne to name Congrong crown prince.
units.literal: Vice Director of the Master of Horses He Ze submitted a memorial asking that Congrong be made crown prince.

units.zh: 是時明宗已病，得澤書不悅，顧左右曰：「群臣欲立太子，吾當養老於河東。」
units.en: Mingzong was already ill; He’s petition angered him, and he told those at his side: “If the court wants a crown prince, I can go grow old in Hedong.”
units.literal: By then Mingzong was already ill; receiving He’s memorial displeased him, and turning to those beside him he said: “The ministers wish to install a crown prince—I ought to retire and grow old in Hedong.”

units.zh: 乃召大臣議立太子事，大臣皆莫敢可否。
units.en: He called the ministers to debate the succession; none dared speak for or against it.
units.literal: He then summoned the ministers to discuss establishing a crown prince; none dared assent or object.

units.zh: 從榮入白曰：「臣聞奸人言，欲立臣為太子，臣實不願也。」
units.en: Congrong entered and said: “I hear schemers want me made heir—I want no part of it.”
units.literal: Congrong came in and reported: “I have heard evil men say they wish to make me crown prince; I truly do not want it.”

units.zh: 明宗曰：「此羣臣之欲爾。」
units.en: Mingzong said: “That is what the ministers want.”
units.literal: Mingzong said: “This is what the ministers want.”

units.zh: 從榮出，見範延光、趙延壽等曰：「諸公議欲立吾為太子，是欲奪吾兵柄而幽之東宮耳。」
units.en: Leaving, Congrong told Fan Yanguang and Zhao Yanshou: “You mean to make me heir so you can take my troops and lock me in the Eastern Palace.”
units.literal: Congrong went out, saw Fan Yanguang, Zhao Yanshou, and others, and said: “Gentlemen, your talk of making me crown prince is really to strip me of my command and shut me away in the Eastern Palace.”

units.zh: 延光等患之，乃加從榮天下兵馬大元帥。
units.en: Alarmed, Yanguang and the rest made Congrong Grand Marshal of All Armies Under Heaven.
units.literal: Yanguang and the others were alarmed and so added to Congrong the title Grand Marshal of All Armies Under Heaven.

units.zh: 有司又言：「元帥或統諸道，或專一面，自前世無天下大元帥之名，其禮無所考按。
units.en: The ministries reported: “Marshals have ruled a circuit or a single front—never before has anyone borne the name Grand Marshal of All Armies Under Heaven, and no rite governs it.
units.literal: The relevant offices further said: “Marshals have governed circuits or held a single frontier—since antiquity there has been no title of Grand Marshal of All Armies Under Heaven, and its protocol has no precedent.

units.zh: 請自節度使以下，凡領兵職者，皆具橐以軍禮庭參；
units.en: From military governors down, every officer with troops should attend the marshal in full kit and military ceremony;
units.literal: We ask that from military governors downward, all who hold military posts come before the marshal with full accoutrements in military ceremony;

units.zh: 其兼同中書門下平章事者，初見亦如之，其後許如客禮。
units.en: chief ministers too on first meeting, then by guest rite.
units.literal: those who also serve as chief ministers shall do the same on first audience, but thereafter may use guest ceremony.

units.zh: 凡元帥府文符行天下，皆用帖。
units.en: All orders from the marshal’s headquarters would circulate as posted notices.
units.literal: All documents from the marshal’s headquarters sent throughout the realm shall use post notes.

units.zh: 又升班在宰相上。」
units.en: His court rank was raised above the chief ministers.”
units.literal: He was also advanced in rank above the chief ministers.”

units.zh: 從榮大宴元帥府，諸將皆有頒給：控鶴、奉聖、嚴衛指揮使，人馬一匹、絹十匹；
units.en: Congrong feasted the marshal’s staff and paid out gifts: Crane Control, Sacred Guard, and Strict Guard commanders each got a horse and ten bolts of silk;
units.literal: Congrong held a great feast at the marshal’s headquarters and gave out rewards to the generals: Crane Control, Sacred Guard, and Strict Guard commanders each received a horse and ten bolts of silk;

units.zh: 其諸軍指揮使，人絹十匹；
units.en: other army commanders, ten bolts apiece;
units.literal: other army commanders, ten bolts each;

units.zh: 都頭已下，七匹至三匹。
units.en: company heads and below, from seven bolts down to three.
units.literal: company heads and below, from seven down to three bolts.

units.zh: 又請嚴衛、捧聖千人為牙兵，每入朝，以數百騎先後，張弓挾矢，馳走道上，見者皆震懾。
units.en: He took a thousand Strict and Sacred Guard troops as his personal guard; each time he came to court, hundreds of riders rode before and behind with strung bows and drawn arrows, thundering down the road until onlookers quailed.
units.literal: He further asked for a thousand Strict Guard and Sacred Guard troops as his personal guard; whenever he entered court, several hundred riders rode ahead and behind, bows strung and arrows ready, galloping along the road—everyone who saw them was struck with terror.

units.zh: 從榮又命其寮屬及四方遊士試作《征淮檄》，陳己所以平一天下之意。
units.en: Congrong had his staff and itinerant literati draft a “Proclamation for the Huai Campaign,” proclaiming his will to pacify the realm.
units.literal: Congrong also ordered his staff and wandering scholars from all quarters to draft a “Proclamation for the Huai Campaign,” setting out his intent to pacify the realm.

units.zh: 言事者請為諸王擇師傅，以加訓導。
units.en: Memorialists asked that tutors be chosen for the princes.
units.literal: Memorialists asked that tutors be chosen for the princes to instruct and guide them.

units.zh: 宰相難其事，因請從榮自擇。
units.en: The chief ministers balked and asked Congrong to choose his own.
units.literal: The chief ministers found the matter difficult and therefore asked Congrong to choose for himself.

units.zh: 從榮乃請翰林學士崔棁、刑部侍郎任贊為元帥判官。
units.en: Congrong named Hanlin Academician Cui Zhuo and Vice Minister Ren Zan marshal adjutants.
units.literal: Congrong then asked Hanlin Academician Cui Zhuo and Vice Minister of Justice Ren Zan to serve as the marshal’s adjutants.

units.zh: 明宗曰：「學士代予言，不可也。」
units.en: Mingzong said: “Academicians speak for me—they cannot serve you.”
units.literal: Mingzong said: “The academicians speak for me—they cannot.”

units.zh: 從榮出而恚曰：「任以元帥而不得請屬寮，非吾所諭也。」
units.en: Congrong left fuming: “You make me marshal but deny me my own staff—that was not the bargain.”
units.literal: Congrong went out enraged and said: “To grant me the marshal’s title yet not let me appoint my own staff—is beyond what I was told could happen.”

units.zh: 將相大臣見從榮權位益隆，而輕脫如此，皆知其禍而莫敢言者。
units.en: Generals and ministers watched Congrong’s power swell and his heedless swagger; all saw the coming ruin, yet none spoke.
units.literal: Generals and ministers saw Congrong’s power ever rising and his recklessness like this; all knew disaster was coming but none dared speak.

units.zh: 惟延光、延壽陰有避禍意，數見明宗，涕泣求解樞密，二人皆引去，而從榮之難作。
units.en: Only Yanguang and Yanshou, hoping to dodge the blow, wept before Mingzong again and again to leave the Bureau of Military Affairs; both stepped down—and Congrong’s disaster began.
units.literal: Only Yanguang and Yanshou secretly meant to escape the coming ruin; they repeatedly saw Mingzong, weeping and begging to be relieved of the Bureau of Military Affairs; both withdrew from office—and Congrong’s calamity began.

units.zh: 十一月戊子，雪，明宗幸宮西士和亭，得傷寒疾。
units.en: On wuzi of the eleventh month it snowed; Mingzong went to Shihe Pavilion west of the palace and caught a chill.
units.literal: On wuzi of the eleventh month, snow; Mingzong visited Shihe Pavilion west of the palace and contracted a chill.

units.zh: 己丑，從榮與樞密使朱弘昭、馮赟入問起居於廣壽殿，帝不能知人。
units.en: On jichou Congrong came with Bureau commissioners Zhu Hongzhao and Feng Yun to ask after Mingzong in Guangshou Hall; the Emperor knew no one.
units.literal: On jichou Congrong entered with Bureau commissioners Zhu Hongzhao and Feng Yun to inquire after the Emperor’s health in Guangshou Hall; the Emperor could not recognize anyone.

units.zh: 王淑妃告曰「從榮在此。」
units.en: Consort Wang said: “Congrong is here.”
units.literal: Consort Wang told him: “Congrong is here.”

units.zh: 又曰：「弘昭等在此。」
units.en: She added: “Hongzhao and the others are here.”
units.literal: She also said: “Hongzhao and the others are here.”

units.zh: 皆不應。
units.en: He did not answer.
units.literal: He did not answer at all.

units.zh: 從榮等去，乃遷於雍和殿，宮中皆慟哭。
units.en: Congrong and the rest withdrew; Mingzong was moved to Yonghe Hall, and the palace wept.
units.literal: Congrong and the others left; he was moved to Yonghe Hall, and the whole palace wailed.

units.zh: 至夜半後，帝蹶然自興於榻，而侍疾者皆去，顧殿上守漏宮女曰：「夜漏幾何？」
units.en: Past midnight Mingzong suddenly sat up; his attendants had all gone; he asked the maid keeping the water clock: “What watch is it?”
units.literal: After midnight the Emperor suddenly sat up on his couch; those tending him had all gone away; he turned to the palace maid keeping the water clock and said: “What hour of the night?”

units.zh: 對曰：「四更矣！」
units.en: She said: “The fourth watch!”
units.literal: She answered: “The fourth watch!”

units.zh: 帝即唾肉如肺者數片，溺涎液斗餘。
units.en: He spat up several pieces of flesh like lung and voided more than a peck of phlegm.
units.literal: The Emperor then expectorated several pieces of flesh like lung tissue and voided more than a peck of saliva.

units.zh: 守漏者曰：「大家省事乎？」
units.en: The maid asked: “Does Your Majesty feel easier?”
units.literal: The clock-keeper said: “Does Your Majesty feel easier?”

units.zh: 曰：「吾不知也。」
units.en: He said: “I do not know.”
units.literal: He said: “I do not know.”

units.zh: 有頃，六宮皆至，曰：「大家還魂矣！」
units.en: Soon the whole inner palace gathered: “His Majesty has come back from death!”
units.literal: Before long the whole inner palace came and cried: “His Majesty has returned from death!”

units.zh: 因進粥一器。
units.en: They brought gruel.
units.literal: They brought him a bowl of gruel.

units.zh: 至旦，疾少愈，而從榮稱疾不朝。
units.en: By dawn he was somewhat better, but Congrong pleaded illness and stayed away from court.
units.literal: By dawn his illness eased somewhat, but Congrong pleaded illness and did not attend court.

units.zh: 初，從榮常忌宋王從厚賢於己，而懼不為嗣。
units.en: Congrong had long resented that the Prince of Song, Conghou, outshone him and feared he would not be heir.
units.literal: From the first Congrong had envied the Prince of Song, Conghou, for being more worthy than himself and feared he would not succeed to the throne.

units.zh: 其平居驕矜自得，及聞人道宋王之善，則愀然有不足之色。
units.en: Proud and self-satisfied in daily life, he darkened whenever anyone praised the Prince of Song.
units.literal: In daily life he was proud and self-satisfied; when he heard men praise the Prince of Song’s virtues he would look crestfallen, as though found wanting.

units.zh: 其入問疾也，見帝已不知人，既去，而聞宮中哭聲，以謂帝已崩矣，乃謀以兵入宮。
units.en: On his sick visit he found Mingzong unrecognizing; leaving, he heard weeping in the palace, took the Emperor for dead, and plotted to march in with troops.
units.literal: When he went to inquire after the Emperor’s health and saw that the Emperor no longer knew anyone, he left; hearing weeping in the palace, he took it that the Emperor had died and plotted to enter the palace with troops.

units.zh: 使其押衙馬處鈞告弘昭等，欲以牙兵入宿衛，問何所可以居者。
units.en: He sent his adjutant Ma Chujun to tell Hongzhao and the rest he meant to quarter his guard in the palace and asked where he should stay.
units.literal: He had his adjutant Ma Chujun tell Hongzhao and the others that he wished to bring his personal guard in as palace guards and asked where he might lodge.

units.zh: 弘昭等對曰：「宮中皆王所可居，王自擇之。」
units.en: Hongzhao and the others said: “Anywhere in the palace is yours, Highness—choose yourself.”
units.literal: Hongzhao and the others replied: “Anywhere in the palace is yours to lodge, Your Highness—choose as you will.”

units.zh: 因私謂處鈞曰：「聖上萬福，王宜竭力忠孝，不可草草。」
units.en: Privately they told Chujun: “His Majesty still lives; serve him with loyalty and filial piety—do nothing rash.”
units.literal: Privately they told Chujun: “His Majesty enjoys full fortune; Your Highness should serve him with all loyalty and filial piety—not rashly.”

units.zh: 處鈞具以告從榮，從榮還遣處鈞語弘昭等曰：「爾輩不念家族乎？」
units.en: Chujun told Congrong everything; Congrong sent him back: “Do you not care for your families?”
units.literal: Chujun reported all this to Congrong, who sent him back to tell Hongzhao and the others: “Do you not care for your families?”

units.zh: 弘昭、赟及宣徽使孟漢瓊等入告王淑妃以謀之，曰：「此事須得侍衛兵為助。」
units.en: Hongzhao, Feng Yun, and Palace Secretariat envoy Meng Hanqiong went to Consort Wang and said: “We will need the palace guard.”
units.literal: Hongzhao, Yun, and Palace Secretariat envoy Meng Hanqiong went to Consort Wang to plan and said: “This will require the help of the palace guard.”

units.zh: 乃召侍衛指揮使康義誠，謀於竹林之下。
units.en: They summoned guard commander Kang Yicheng and plotted under the bamboo grove.
units.literal: They summoned guard commander Kang Yicheng and plotted beneath the bamboo grove.

units.zh: 義誠有子在秦王府，不敢決其謀，謂弘昭曰：「仆為將校，惟公所使爾！」
units.en: Yicheng had a son in the Prince of Qin’s service and would not choose sides; he told Hongzhao: “I am a soldier—I obey your command!”
units.literal: Yicheng had a son in the Prince of Qin’s household and dared not decide on the plot; he told Hongzhao: “I am a soldier—I do only as you order!”

units.zh: 弘昭大懼。
units.en: Hongzhao was terrified.
units.literal: Hongzhao was greatly afraid.

units.zh: 明日，從榮遣馬處鈞告馮赟曰：「吾今日入居興聖宮。」
units.en: Next day Congrong sent Ma Chujun to Feng Yun: “Today I move into Xingsheng Palace.”
units.literal: The next day Congrong sent Ma Chujun to tell Feng Yun: “Today I am entering and taking up residence in Xingsheng Palace.”

units.zh: 又告義誠，義誠許諾。
units.en: He told Yicheng too, and Yicheng agreed.
units.literal: He also told Yicheng, and Yicheng assented.

units.zh: 赟即馳入內，見義誠及弘昭、漢瓊等坐中興殿閣議事，赟責義誠曰：「主上所以畜養吾徒者，為今日爾！
units.en: Feng Yun galloped in at once; finding Yicheng, Hongzhao, and Hanqiong in council at Zhongxing Hall, he rebuked Yicheng: “His Majesty kept us for this day!
units.literal: Yun immediately galloped inside; finding Yicheng and Hongzhao and Hanqiong seated in Zhongxing Hall discussing affairs, he rebuked Yicheng: “His Majesty kept us alive for this very day!

units.zh: 今安危之機，間不容發，奈何以子故懷顧望，使秦王得至此門，主上安所歸乎？
units.en: Life and death hang on a breath—how can you waver for your son and let the Prince of Qin reach this gate? Where will His Majesty go?
units.literal: Now the moment of life and death allows no delay—how can you hesitate for your son’s sake and let the Prince of Qin reach this gate? Where will His Majesty find safety?

units.zh: 吾輩復有種乎？」
units.en: Will any of us survive?”
units.literal: Will any seed of us remain?”

units.zh: 漢瓊曰：「賤命不足惜，吾自率兵拒之。」
units.en: Hanqiong said: “My life is nothing—I will lead troops to stop him myself.”
units.literal: Hanqiong said: “My worthless life does not matter—I will lead troops to resist him myself.”

units.zh: 即入見曰：「從榮反，兵已攻端門。」
units.en: He went in at once: “Congrong has rebelled; his troops are at Duan Gate.”
units.literal: He entered at once to report: “Congrong has rebelled; troops are already attacking Duan Gate.”

units.zh: 宮中相顧號泣。
units.en: In the palace they stared at one another and wept.
units.literal: In the palace they looked at one another and wept aloud.

units.zh: 明宗問弘昭等曰：「實有之乎？」
units.en: Mingzong asked Hongzhao and the others: “Is it true?”
units.literal: Mingzong asked Hongzhao and the others: “Is it true?”

units.zh: 對曰：「有之。」
units.en: They said: “It is.”
units.literal: They answered: “It is.”

units.zh: 明宗以手指天泣下，良久曰：「義誠自處置，毋令震動京師。」
units.en: Mingzong pointed heavenward and wept; after a long silence he said: “Let Yicheng deal with it—do not shake the capital.”
units.literal: Mingzong pointed to heaven and wept; after a long while he said: “Let Yicheng handle it—do not let the capital be shaken.”

units.zh: 潞王子重吉在側，明宗曰：「吾與爾父起微賤，至取天下，數救我危窘。
units.en: Chongji, son of the Prince of Lu, stood beside him; Mingzong said: “Your father and I rose from nothing and took the realm; again and again he pulled me from danger.
units.literal: Chongji, son of the Prince of Lu, was at his side; Mingzong said: “Your father and I rose from nothing to take the realm; again and again he saved me from peril.

units.zh: 從榮得何氣力，而作此惡事！
units.en: What strength has Congrong to do this evil!
units.literal: What strength has Congrong to do this evil deed!

units.zh: 爾亟以兵守諸門。」
units.en: Go now and hold the gates with troops.”
units.literal: Go at once and hold the gates with troops.”

units.zh: 重吉即以控鶴兵守宮門。
units.en: Chongji manned the palace gates with Crane Control troops.
units.literal: Chongji immediately manned the palace gates with Crane Control troops.

units.zh: 是日，從榮自河南府擁兵千人以出。
units.en: That day Congrong marched out of Henan with a thousand men.
units.literal: That day Congrong came forth from Henan with a thousand troops.

units.zh: 從榮寮屬甚眾，而正直之士多見惡，其尤所惡者劉贊、王居敏，而所昵者劉陟、高輦。
units.en: Congrong’s staff was large; upright men he mostly despised—above all Liu Zan and Wang Jumin; he favored Liu Zhi and Gao Nian.
units.literal: Congrong’s staff was large; upright men were mostly hated—most hated of all Liu Zan and Wang Jumin; those he favored were Liu Zhi and Gao Nian.

units.zh: 從榮兵出，與陟、輦並轡耳語，行至天津橋南，指日景謂輦曰：「明日而今，誅王居敏矣！」
units.en: Marching out, Congrong rode beside Zhi and Nian, whispering; south of Tianjin Bridge he pointed at the sun’s shadow and told Nian: “This time tomorrow Wang Jumin dies!”
units.literal: Marching out, Congrong rode beside Zhi and Nian, whispering; south of Tianjin Bridge he pointed at the sun’s shadow and told Nian: “This time tomorrow Wang Jumin dies!”

units.zh: 因陣兵橋北，下據胡床而坐，使人召康義誠。
units.en: He formed ranks north of the bridge, sat on a camp stool, and sent for Kang Yicheng.
units.literal: He then drew up troops north of the bridge, dismounted and sat on a folding camp chair, and sent men to summon Kang Yicheng.

units.zh: 而端門已閉，叩左掖門，亦閉，而於門隙中見捧聖指揮使朱弘實率騎兵從北來，即馳告從榮。
units.en: Duan Gate was shut; the Left Flank Gate too; through a crack he saw Sacred Guard commander Zhu Hongshi riding down from the north and galloped to warn Congrong.
units.literal: But Duan Gate was closed; he knocked at the Left Flank Gate—also closed; through a gap in the gate he saw Sacred Guard commander Zhu Hongshi leading cavalry from the north and galloped to tell Congrong.

units.zh: 從榮驚懼，索鐵厭心，自調弓矢。
units.en: Congrong panicked, called for iron arrowheads, and strung his bow himself.
units.literal: Congrong was alarmed and afraid; he called for iron arrowheads and strung his bow himself.

units.zh: 皇城使安從益率騎兵三百沖之，從榮兵射之，從益稍卻。
units.en: Imperial City envoy An Congyi charged with three hundred horse; Congrong’s men shot at him and Congyi gave ground.
units.literal: Imperial City envoy An Congyi led three hundred cavalry in a charge; Congrong’s troops shot at them and Congyi fell back somewhat.

units.zh: 弘實騎兵五百自左掖門出，方渡河，而後軍來者甚眾，從榮乃走歸河南府，其判官任贊已下皆走出定鼎門，牙兵劫嘉善坊而潰。
units.en: Hongshi came out the Left Flank Gate with five hundred horse; as they crossed the river reinforcements poured in; Congrong fled to Henan; adjutants Ren Zan and the rest ran out Dingding Gate; his guard looted Jiashan Ward and scattered.
units.literal: Hongshi with five hundred cavalry came out the Left Flank Gate; just as they were crossing the river a great host came up behind; Congrong fled back to Henan Prefecture; his adjutants Ren Zan and those below all ran out Dingding Gate; his personal guard plundered Jiashan Ward and broke apart.

units.zh: 從榮夫妻匿床下，從益殺之。
units.en: Congrong and his wife hid under a bed; Congyi killed them.
units.literal: Congrong and his wife hid under a bed; Congyi killed them.

units.zh: 明宗聞從榮已死，悲咽幾墮於榻，絕而蘇者再。
units.en: When he heard Congrong was dead, Mingzong wept until he nearly fell from the couch; twice he fainted and came back.
units.literal: Hearing Congrong was dead, Mingzong sobbed until he nearly fell from his couch; twice he lost consciousness and revived.

units.zh: 馮道率百寮入見，明宗曰：「吾家事若此，慚見群臣！」
units.en: Feng Dao led the hundred officials in; Mingzong said: “My house has come to this—I am ashamed to face you!”
units.literal: Feng Dao led the hundred officials in audience; Mingzong said: “My family affairs have come to this—I am ashamed to face you all!”

units.zh: 君臣相顧，泣下沾襟。
units.en: Sovereign and ministers looked at one another; tears soaked their robes.
units.literal: Ministers and sovereign looked at one another; tears soaked their robes.

units.zh: 從榮二子尚幼，皆從死。
units.en: Congrong’s two young sons died with him.
units.literal: Congrong’s two sons were still young; both died with him.

units.zh: 後六日而明宗崩。
units.en: Six days later Mingzong died.
units.literal: Six days later Mingzong died.

units.zh: 明宗兄弟皆不見于世家，而有姪四人，曰：從璨、從璋、從溫、從敏。
units.en: Mingzong's brothers are missing from the genealogies, but four nephews are recorded: Congcan, Congzhang, Congwen, and Congmin.
units.literal: Mingzong's brothers do not appear in the genealogies, but he had four nephews: Congcan, Congzhang, Congwen, and Congmin.

units.zh: 明宗兄弟皆不見於世家，而有侄四人，曰從璨、從璋、從溫、從敏。
units.en: Mingzong’s brothers are missing from the genealogies, but four nephews are recorded: Congcan, Congzhang, Congwen, and Congmin.
units.literal: Mingzong’s brothers do not appear in the genealogies, but he had four nephews: Congcan, Congzhang, Congwen, and Congmin.

units.zh: 從璨初為右衛大將軍，安重誨用事，自諸王將相皆下之，從璨為人剛猛，不能少屈，而性倜儻，輕財好施，重誨忌之。
units.en: Congcan first served as Right Guard grand general; An Chonghui ruled the court and even princes and ministers bowed to him; Congcan was hard and proud, open-handed and bold, and Chonghui hated him.
units.literal: Congcan was at first Right Guard grand general; An Chonghui wielded power and even princes and chief ministers bowed to him; Congcan was fierce and unyielding, generous and free-handed, and Chonghui resented him.

units.zh: 明宗幸汴州，以從璨為大內皇城使。
units.en: When Mingzong visited Bian, he made Congcan grand envoy of the inner imperial city.
units.literal: When Mingzong visited Bianzhou he made Congcan grand envoy of the inner imperial city.

units.zh: 嘗於會節園飲，酒酣，戲登禦榻，重誨奏其事，貶房州司戶參軍，賜死。
units.en: Drunk in Festival Garden he climbed onto the imperial couch in jest; Chonghui reported it; he was demoted to Fangzhou adjutant and granted death.
units.literal: Once drinking in Festival Garden, drunk he playfully mounted the imperial couch; Chonghui reported it; he was demoted to military adjutant of Fangzhou and granted death.

units.zh: 重誨見誅，詔復其官，贈太保。
units.en: After Chonghui’s execution an edict restored his rank and posthumously made him Grand Guardian.
units.literal: When Chonghui was executed an edict restored his office and posthumously made him Grand Guardian.

units.zh: 從璋字子良，少善騎射。
units.en: Congzhang, styled Ziliang, was skilled in horsemanship and archery from youth.
units.literal: Congzhang, style Ziliang, was skilled in horsemanship and archery from youth.

units.zh: 莊宗時，將兵戍常山，聞明宗兵變于魏，乃亦起兵據邢州。
units.en: Under Zhuangzong he garrisoned Changshan; hearing of Mingzong's mutiny at Wei, he too raised troops and seized Xingzhou.
units.literal: Under Zhuangzong he commanded troops garrisoning Changshan; hearing Mingzong's troops mutiny at Wei, he too raised troops and seized Xingzhou.

units.zh: 明宗即位，以為捧聖左廂都指揮使，改皇城使，領饒州刺史，拜彰國軍節度使，徙鎮義成。
units.en: When Mingzong succeeded he was made commander of the Sacred Guard's left wing, then imperial city envoy, prefect of Raozhou, governor of Zhangguo, and later transferred to Yicheng.
units.literal: When Mingzong took the throne he was made commander of the left wing of the Sacred Guard, then grand envoy of the imperial city, prefect of Raozhou, military governor of Zhangguo, and transferred to govern Yicheng.

units.zh: 明宗幸汴州，從璋欲率民為貢獻，其從事諫以為不可，從璋怒，引弓欲射之，坐罷為右驍衞上將軍。
units.en: When Mingzong visited Bian, Congzhang meant to lead the people in tribute; his aide protested; Congzhang drew his bow in rage and was demoted to senior general of the Right Martial Guard.
units.literal: When Mingzong visited Bianzhou, Congzhang wished to lead the people in tribute; his staff officer remonstrated that it was improper; Congzhang in anger drew his bow to shoot him and was demoted to senior general of the Right Martial Guard.

units.zh: 居久之，出鎮保義，徙河中。
units.en: After a time he was sent to govern Baoyi, then transferred to Hezhong.
units.literal: After a long while he was sent out to govern Baoyi and then transferred to Hezhong.

units.zh: 長興四年夏，封洋王。
units.en: In the summer of Changxing 4 he was made Prince of Yang.
units.literal: In summer of Changxing 4 he was enfeoffed Prince of Yang.

units.zh: 晉高祖立，徙鎮威勝，降封隴西郡公。
units.en: When Jin Gaozu rose he was moved to Weisheng and demoted to Duke of Longxi.
units.literal: When Jin Gaozu took the throne he was transferred to govern Weisheng and demoted to Duke of Longxi commandery.

units.zh: 從璋為人貪鄙，自鎮保義，始折節自脩，在南陽頗有遺愛。
units.en: Congzhang was greedy and coarse; from his time at Baoyi he began to reform himself and won goodwill at Nanyang.
units.literal: Congzhang was greedy and base by nature; from his governorship of Baoyi he began to restrain himself and cultivate virtue, and at Nanyang left considerable goodwill.

units.zh: 天福二年卒，年五十一。
units.en: He died in Tianfu 2 at the age of fifty-one.
units.literal: He died in Tianfu 2 at fifty-one.

units.zh: 從溫字德基，初為北京副留守。
units.en: Congwen, styled Deji, was first deputy commissioner of the Northern Capital.
units.literal: Congwen, style Deji, was at first deputy military commissioner of the Northern Capital.

units.zh: 歷安國、忠武、義武、成德、武寧五節度使，封兗王。
units.en: He governed five circuits in turn—Anguo, Zhongwu, Yiwu, Chengde, and Wuning—and was enfeoffed Prince of Yan.
units.literal: He served successively as military governor of five circuits—Anguo, Zhongwu, Yiwu, Chengde, and Wuning—and was enfeoffed Prince of Yan.

units.zh: 晉高祖立，復為忠武軍節度使。
units.en: When Jin Gaozu took the throne he was again made governor of Zhongwu.
units.literal: When Jin Gaozu took the throne he was again made military governor of Zhongwu.

units.zh: 從溫為人貪鄙，多作天子器服以自僭，宗族、賓客諫之，不聽，其妻關氏大呼於牙門曰：「從溫欲反，而造天子服器。」
units.en: Congwen was greedy and coarse; he forged imperial robes and vessels; kin and guests warned him in vain; his wife Lady Guan shouted at the gate: “Congwen means to rebel—see the Son of Heaven’s gear he is making.”
units.literal: Congwen was greedy and vulgar; he made much imperial regalia to usurp prerogatives; clansmen and guests remonstrated but he would not listen; his wife Lady Guan cried out at the military gate: “Congwen means to rebel—look at him forging the Son of Heaven’s robes and vessels.”

units.zh: 從溫大恐，乃悉毀之。
units.en: Terrified, Congwen destroyed them all.
units.literal: Congwen was greatly frightened and destroyed them all.

units.zh: 明宗諸子八人，至晉出帝時六已亡歿，惟從溫、從敏在，太后常曰：「吾惟有一兄，豈可繩之以法！」
units.en: Of Mingzong’s eight sons, six were dead by the Deposed Emperor’s day; only Congwen and Congmin remained; the empress dowager often said: “I have only this one elder kinsman—how can I punish him by law!”
units.literal: Of Mingzong’s eight sons, by the time of Jin’s Deposed Emperor six had died; only Congwen and Congmin remained; the empress dowager often said: “I have only this one elder kinsman—how can I bind him with the law!”

units.zh: 從溫由此益驕。
units.en: Congwen grew bolder still.
units.literal: Congwen grew all the bolder for it.

units.zh: 嘗誣親吏薛仁嗣為盜，悉籍沒其家貲數千萬。
units.en: Once he falsely accused his clerk Xue Rensi of theft and seized his household wealth—tens of millions.
units.literal: Once he falsely accused his personal clerk Xue Rensi of theft and confiscated his household wealth, tens of millions.

units.zh: 仁嗣等詣闕自訴，事下有司，從溫具伏。
units.en: Rensi and the others appealed at court; the case went to the ministries and Congwen confessed in full.
units.literal: Rensi and others went to court to plead their case; the matter was referred to the offices and Congwen fully confessed.

units.zh: 出帝懼傷太后意，釋之而不問。
units.en: The Deposed Emperor, fearing to hurt the empress dowager, released him without further inquiry.
units.literal: The Deposed Emperor feared wounding the empress dowager’s feelings and released him without inquiry.

units.zh: 開運二年，徙河陽三城，卒於官。
units.en: In Kaiyun 2 he was moved to the Heyang three cities and died in office.
units.literal: In Kaiyun 2 he was transferred to the Heyang three cities and died in office.

units.zh: 是時從璋子重俊為虢州刺史，坐臟，亦以太后故，罪其判官高獻而已。
units.en: Then Congzhang’s son Chongjun was prefect of Guo; convicted of graft; again for the empress dowager’s sake only his adjutant Gao Xian was punished.
units.literal: At that time Congzhang’s son Chongjun was prefect of Guo; convicted of graft; again for the empress dowager’s sake only his adjutant Gao Xian was punished.

units.zh: 重俊復為商州刺史。
units.en: Chongjun was again made prefect of Shang.
units.literal: Chongjun was again made prefect of Shang.

units.zh: 坐與其妹奸及殺其仆孫漢榮掠其妻，賜死。
units.en: Convicted of lying with his sister and of killing his servant Sun Hanrong to take his wife, he was granted death.
units.literal: Convicted of incest with his sister and of killing his servant Sun Hanrong to seize his wife, he was granted death.

units.zh: 從敏字叔達，為人沉厚寡言，善騎射。
units.en: Congmin, styled Shuda, was grave, quiet, and skilled in horsemanship and archery.
units.literal: Congmin, styled Shuda, was deep, steady, and sparing of speech, skilled in horsemanship and archery.

units.zh: 初從莊宗為馬步軍都指揮使兼行軍司馬，明宗入立，遷皇城使、保義軍節度使，與討王都。
units.en: He first served Zhuangzong as commander of horse and foot and army marshal; when Mingzong succeeded he became imperial city envoy and governor of Baoyi and joined the campaign against Wang Du.
units.literal: At first he followed Zhuangzong as commander of horse and foot armies and concurrent army marshal; when Mingzong took the throne he was made imperial city envoy and military governor of Baoyi and joined the campaign against Wang Du.

units.zh: 歷鎮橫海、義武、成德、歸德、保義、昭義、河陽，封涇王。
units.en: He governed Henghai, Yiwu, Chengde, Guide, Baoyi, Zhaoyi, and Heyang in turn and was enfeoffed Prince of Jing.
units.literal: He governed in succession Henghai, Yiwu, Chengde, Guide, Baoyi, Zhaoyi, and Heyang, and was enfeoffed Prince of Jing.

units.zh: 漢高祖時，為西京留守，封秦國公。
units.en: Under Han Gaozu he was regent of the Western Capital and made Duke of Qin.
units.literal: Under Han Gaozu he was Western Capital regent and enfeoffed Duke of Qin.

units.zh: 周廣順元年卒，贈中書令，謚曰恭惠。
units.en: He died in Zhou's first year Guangshun; posthumously made Director of the Secretariat and named Gonghui.
units.literal: He died in Guangshun 1 of Zhou; posthumously made Director of the Secretariat with posthumous name Gonghui.
